title: Gears of War: E-Day sistem gereksinimleri açıklandı
summary: Gears of War: E-Day, donanım düzeyinde ışın izleme desteğine sahip ekran kartı zorunluluğu ve SSD'de 115 GB boş alan gerektiriyor.
body:
Gears of War: E-Day sistem gereksinimleri, oyunun çıkışı yaklaşırken geliştirici stüdyo The Coalition tarafından paylaşıldı. PC Gamer'ın aktardığına göre, 6 Ekim'de tam sürümüyle oyuncularla buluşmaya hazırlanan yapım, donanım düzeyinde ışın izleme (ray tracing) destekleyen bir ekran kartını zorunlu kılıyor.

## Donanım ve depolama detayları

PC Gamer'ın paylaştığı bilgilere göre, oyunun en düşük ayarlarda çalışabilmesi için RTX 2060 veya RX 6600 seviyesinde bir ekran kartı gerekiyor. 4K Ultra ayarlarda ise RTX 5070 Ti veya RX 7900 XT ekran kartlarının yanı sıra sekiz veya daha fazla çekirdeğe sahip işlemciler öneriliyor. Depolama tarafında ise oyuncuların **115 GB** boş alana sahip bir katı hal sürücüsüne (SSD) ihtiyaç duyacağı belirtiliyor.

## Teknik destekler

Gears of War: E-Day, çıkış gününde DLSS 4.5, AMD FSR 4 ve Intel XeSS 3.0 teknolojilerini destekleyecek. Bellek tarafında ise minimum 12 GB RAM ile oyunun çalıştırılabileceği ifade ediliyor.

**Neden önemli?** Oyuncuların Gears of War: E-Day deneyimini yaşayabilmesi için ışın izleme özellikli bir ekran kartına ve SSD depolamaya sahip olması şart koşuluyor.

source_texts.text:
October 1, 2026: With the game in its early access period, you can read our review in progress right now. Story short: the shooting is good, but the campaign is a bit of a slog. If you're wondering if your rig can handle it, you can check out the full system requirements below.
Gears of War: E-Day is set to launch on October 6, though the early access period is live right now. In the lead-up to launch, The Coalition has posted expanded system requirements for the upcoming bug blast. These include what the game asks of your rig for top performance on the top settings—it's not easygoing, to say the least—but providing your GPU is at least capable of ray tracing, most should get by fine on medium settings.
An RTX 5070 Ti or RX 7900 XT will be required in order to run the game at 4K with the Ultra preset enabled. This is targeting a steady 60 fps, and I would assume, from the 12 GB of VRAM noted in the table below, that one should be able to swing it on a lower-end card with some assistance from upscaling.
Gears of War: E-Day supports DLSS 4.5, AMD FSR 4, and Intel XeSS 3.0 at launch, so we're not short of options there.
Otherwise, GPU demands are similar to those we saw back in June: an RTX 2060 or RX 6600 at a minimum, or an RTX 3060 Ti/6700 XT as recommended. It's only at 4K Ultra that demands seem to really ramp up. Though there is a blanket requirement for a ray tracing-capable graphics card to play Gears of War: E-Day. The devs explicitly say so on the new system requirements table:
"A hardware ray tracing capable graphics card is required. Graphics cards without dedicated hardware ray tracing support are not support."
You can't ask for it to be clearer than that. The game comes with ray-traced reflections, shadows, and global illumination.
CPU demands are pretty wide-ranging: from a mere Ryzen 5 2600X at a minimum, to a Ryzen 5 5600 as recommended. For 4K Ultra, it looks like eight cores or more are best; furthermore, a 3D V-Cache chip is recommended: the AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D. The studio also suggests an Intel Core i7 14700K. I'd assume newer Arrow Lake chips would suffice, too, despite their slightly weaker performance at times.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
RAM requirements are modest enough, even at 4K, at a mere 16 GB. Though only 12 GB are required to play the game. You'll have to make way for the game on an SSD, however, as 115 GB of storage space is required. That does actually need to be a solid state drive, so sayeth the devs.
Jacob has been writing about PC hardware and technology for over eight years. He earned his first byline at PCGamesN before joining PC Gamer. He spends most of his time building PCs, running benchmarks, and trying his best to learn Linux.
